Main.sentence: Julian Emanuel Zelizer (born 1969) is an American professor of ___E:political history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_history)___ and author at ___E:Princeton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University)___ .
Zelizer focuses on the second half of the twentieth century and the twenty-first century, and has authored or co-authored several books about American political history.

Raised in ___E:Metuchen, New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metuchen,_New_Jersey)___ , Zelizer was educated at ___E:Metuchen High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metuchen_High_School)___ , a comprehensive public high school,  followed by ___E:Brandeis University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandeis_University)___ .
He obtained a ___E:PhD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PhD)___ in History from ___E:Johns Hopkins University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University)___ .
Zelizer has contributed to ___E:CNN.com U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN.com)___ and ___E:The Atlantic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic_(magazine))___ .
He is a regular commentator on news programs and has appeared in several documentary films.
He penned the introduction to a 2016 edition of the ___E:Kerner report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerner_Commission)___ .
He is the ___E:Malcolm Stevenson Forbes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Stevenson_Forbes)___ Professor of History and Public Policy.

He has twice won the ___E:D. B. Hardeman Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._B._Hardeman_Prize)___ , for Taxing America: Wilbur D. Mills, Congress, and the State, 1945–1975 and The Fierce Urgency of Now: Lyndon Johnson, Congress, and the Battle for the Great Society .
Fault Lines: A History of the United States Since 1974 , co-authored with ___E:Kevin M. Kruse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_M._Kruse)___ , received wide critical acclaim.

Zelizer's book, Burning Down the House: Newt Gingrich, the Fall of a Speaker, and the Rise of the New Republican Party, was called "insightful" by The New York Times , which also recognized it as one of the "100 Notable Books of 2020".
The Washington Post wrote that it was "engaging" and "timely".

In 2025, Zelizer began a ___E:Substack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substack)___ publication online that is entitled, The Long View , and is intended to provide a historical perspective to breaking news that enables free and paid subscribers to gain a better understanding of current events.

Zelizer is the son of the Princeton ___E:sociologist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociologist)___ ___E:Viviana Zelizer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viviana_Zelizer)___ and Gerald L. Zelizer,   a notable ___E:Metuchen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metuchen,_New_Jersey)___ ___E:rabbi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbi)___ .

In 1996, he married Nora Kay Moran at ___E:Congregation Adas Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adas_Israel_Congregation_(Washington,_D.C.))___ in ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , presided over by his father.

In 2012, he married fellow historian ___E:Meg Jacobs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Jacobs)___ at the ___E:Synagogue for the Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TriBeCa_Synagogue)___ in ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ , again presided over by his father.
In addition to authoring the books listed above, Zelizer has edited or co-edited a number of books including, most recently, Our Nation at Risk: Election Integrity as a National Security Issue .
